## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
- Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
- Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 3D Universe Sandbox-style game for phone/tablet in the existing repo, with responsive touch controls and high visual polish.
- Game is branded **ORBITALIS — Gravity Sandbox**, a living solar-system builder/simulator with five sequential trials.

## Requirements
- 3D game, phone/tablet, responsive touch layouts and safe areas.
- Must be playable now; no clarifying questions; note reasonable assumptions on finish.
- For self-checks, save small JPEGs (`.jpg`, viewport max 1280px wide) and read only latest images; full-size PNGs only for fine detail.

## Decisions
- Vanilla HTML/CSS/JS + locally vendored Three.js r170, avoiding remote runtime dependencies.
- Local `Space Grotesk` and `IBM Plex Mono` fonts, locally generated procedural planet/star/ring/glow textures.
- Circular orbital insertion for player-created worlds; N-body star + weak planet gravity for stability.
- Moons are held on stable parent-relative “rails” so they remain readable and do not accidentally destroy the starting system.
- Trials: `First Light` (deploy any world), `Goldilocks` (terrestrial at 15.8–22.5 orbit), `Ring Bearer` (Jovian beyond 27), `Lunar Tether` (add moon), `Collision Course` (comet collision).
- Comets are predictive-targeted at the selected world; selecting a target first is the intended flow.
- Desktop auto-selects Pelagos for showcase; mobile does not to preserve screen space.
- Initial system: Cinder (desert, r10.6), Pelagos (ocean, r17.2, moon Rill r3.7), Aurelia (ringed gas, r27.0), Nyx (ice, r41.5).
- Kept postprocessing bloom for visual quality; software renderer is slow (~5–10 fps under llvmpipe) but real mobile GPUs should be fine. Adaptive quality was considered but not implemented.

## Work State
### Completed
- Full app scaffold: `index.html`, `src/main.js`, `src/universe.js`, `src/textures.js`, `src/audio.js`, `src/style.css`.
- Locally vendored Three.js, OrbitControls, postprocessing (`EffectComposer`, `RenderPass`, `UnrealBloomPass`, `OutputPass`, shaders) and fonts under `vendor/`.
- Procedural solar system, star shader, planet textures, rings, moons, asteroid belt, starfield/nebula, trails, selection reticle, camera orbit/pinch/focus.
- Touch/mouse interaction, adding worlds/moons/comets, boost/delete/focus, pause and 1×/2×/4× time controls, reset flow, sound toggle, help modal, completion modal.
- Trial progression verified end-to-end via `window.orbitalis` automation: trial scores 120/180/260/320/500, final 1,380, completion modal appears.
- Desktop and mobile screenshots visually reviewed; layout generally polished.
- Added local favicon to remove 404.
- Fixed unstable initial system by setting `PLANET_GRAVITY_SCALE = 0.16` and skipping moon-vs-non-comet collisions; verified stable to sim time ~92s.
- Adjusted mobile selected-card bottom to `123px` so it no longer sits under the time cluster; hid controls hint on selection.
- Lightened body-orb previews.

### Active
- Just took `screenshots/mobile-selected3.jpg` after mobile selected-card/time-cluster fix; needs visual check.
- Need final verification of desktop/mobile screenshots, controls, forge, selected card, and official capture script.
- Need possibly add adaptive performance fallback for software renderers.
- Need update `README.md` with game description/controls and assumptions.

### Blocked
- None.

## Next Move
1. Read `screenshots/mobile-selected3.jpg` to verify the selected card now clears the time cluster.
2. Check desktop selected card actions no longer wrap (`white-space: nowrap` fix) and re-check overall scene.
3. Test touch-like click selection, forge flow, add moon, comet collision, pause/speed, help/completion modals at 390×844 and 768×1024.
4. Run official capture via `CAPTURE_URL=http://localhost:3000 CAPTURE_DIR=screenshots ./capture.sh` and inspect outputs.
5. Consider adaptive bloom/pixel-ratio fallback for low-FPS software renderers; ensure sim time uses `rawDt` cap `0.1`.
6. Update `README.md` with title, description, controls, trial list, and brief assumptions.
7. Final syntax check (`node --check`), remove debug screenshots if desired, stop the dev server if appropriate, report completion.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: app markup, UI panels, forge sheet, help/completion modals, import map.
- `src/main.js`: game loop UI orchestration, trials, toasts, forge, selection, keyboard/touch bindings, `window.orbitalis` test API.
- `src/universe.js`: Three.js scene, physics, bodies, moons, comets, camera, postprocessing, collision/particles.
- `src/textures.js`: procedural planet/cloud/ring/glow/reticle textures and `BODY_TYPES`.
- `src/style.css`: full responsive UI, mobile/tablet media queries, animations.
- `src/audio.js`: procedural ambient/UI/impact audio.
- `vendor/three/`: local Three.js core, controls, postprocessing and shaders.
- `vendor/fonts/`: local Space Grotesk and IBM Plex Mono woff2 files.
- `screenshots/mobile-selected3.jpg`: latest unreviewed mobile selection screenshot.

# ORBITALIS — Gravity Sandbox

A living solar-system sandbox for phone, tablet, and desktop. Sculpt a system around the star Helios, drop new worlds into orbit, tether moons, and steer a comet into anything that gets in your way.

Built with vanilla HTML/CSS/JavaScript and a locally vendored Three.js r170. Every texture, font, and shader is served from this repository, so the game runs with no network access once loaded.

![ORBITALIS gameplay](screenshots/desktop5.jpg)

## Play

Serve the project folder over any static HTTP server, then open the local URL.

```bash
python3 -m http.server 3000
# http://localhost:3000
```

The simulator is tuned for touch first, but works with mouse and keyboard too. Safe-area insets are respected on notched phones.

## Controls

| Action | Touch | Mouse / keyboard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Orbit camera | Drag empty space | Drag empty space |
| Zoom | Pinch | Scroll wheel |
| Select a world | Tap the world or its label | Click |
| Create a world | **WORLD** in the dock | `W` |
| Launch a comet | **COMET** in the dock | `C` |
| Add a moon | **MOON** in the dock | `M` |
| Focus selection | **FOCUS** in the dock | `F` |
| Pause / resume | Time cluster play button | `Space` |
| Time warp | `1×` / `2×` / `4×` | `1` / `2` / `4` |
| Reset system | **RESET** twice | `R` twice |
| Help | `?` in the top bar | `H` |

Comets are predictive: select a world first, then launch a comet and it will curve toward that target.

## The five trials

1. **First Light** — deploy any world. `+120`
2. **Goldilocks** — place a terrestrial world inside the habitable ring. `+180`
3. **Ring Bearer** — raise a Jovian-class gas giant beyond the frost line. `+260`
4. **Lunar Tether** — bind a moon to one of your worlds. `+320`
5. **Collision Course** — drive a comet into a world. `+500`

Completing all five reveals the final system score and a free-play sandbox. Trials can be replayed by resetting the system.

## What is simulated

- A central star with custom shader corona, arcs, and sprite glows.
- N-body star gravity plus a softened, weak planet-to-planet attraction; new worlds are inserted on circular orbits so the starting system stays stable.
- Moons ride stable parent-relative rails, keeping them readable and preventing accidental system-wide disruption.
- Comets use predictive targeting and can collide with worlds, spawning impact particles and a camera shake.
- Procedural planet surfaces, cloud layers, ring systems, asteroid belt, starfield, and nebula are generated at runtime from seeded noise.
- Adaptive quality drops render resolution and, if needed, bloom on devices that cannot sustain a smooth frame rate.

## Project layout

```text
index.html          UI shell, forge, help and completion modals
src/main.js         trial logic, UI orchestration, input bindings, test hooks
src/universe.js     Three.js scene, physics, camera, post-processing
src/textures.js     procedural textures and body definitions
src/audio.js        procedural ambient and impact sound
src/style.css       responsive layout and visual system
vendor/             local Three.js build, addons, shaders, and fonts
```

## Notes and assumptions

- The starting system is intentionally gentle: **Cinder**, **Pelagos** (with moon **Rill**), **Aurelia**, and **Nyx** orbit Helios on stable rails.
- Orbital distances are game units displayed as AU; the habitable ring maps to the 15.8–22.5 unit band used by the Goldilocks trial.
- Phone and tablet layouts are the primary target; desktop auto-selects Pelagos on load for a populated first view.
- Audio starts only after the first interaction, as required by mobile browsers.
- `capture.sh` and `start.sh` expect the OMGithub runtime environment; any static server works for local play.

- A complete Three.js solar-system sandbox with a shader star, procedural planets, rings, moons, asteroid belt, nebula, bloom, trails, and impact effects.
